completeness_gaps: No dedicated Information Disclosure track (source-code disclosure via .git/.svn, backup files like config.bak, verbose stack traces, /debug or /actuator/env leaks, versioned Swagger/OpenAPI leaks) — PortSwigger Academy has this as a first-class topic.

No dedicated Path Traversal / LFI category (only mixed into command-injection-upload-fileread). PortSwigger has it as its own track with 6+ progression labs (encoded ../, null-byte, chroot bypass, /proc/self/environ).
No dedicated CORS misconfiguration category (null origin trust, regex wildcarding, credentialed reflect-origin, cache-based CORS ATO). Currently only 1 sub-lab under client-side.
No dedicated Clickjacking / UI-redressing category (frame busting bypass, target-elem overlay, drag-and-drop clickjacking, cursor-jacking). PortSwigger has 5+ progression labs.

No dedicated CSRF category (SameSite=None, token-in-body vs cookie, referer-check bypass, method override, JSON CSRF via text/plain, GET-triggered mutations) — currently scattered across client-side and hackerone/yeswehack tracks.
No dedicated HTTP Host Header Attacks category (password-reset poisoning, virtual-host confusion, cache poisoning via Host, absolute-URL rewriting) — PortSwigger topic missing.

Web LLM attacks are drastically underrepresented: only 2 labs (indirect prompt injection + tool hijack). Missing: direct prompt injection with jailbreaks, insecure LLM output handling, unbounded token consumption / model DoS, LLM SSRF via tool selection, agent memory poisoning, RAG index poisoning at scale, MCP server abuse, function-calling schema abuse, prompt leak via completion sampling.
No dedicated Session Management track (fixation, insufficient rotation, sticky cookies, JWT ATO via session-store confusion, revocation gaps). WSTG v4.2 requires this.
OWASP A04 Insecure Design has no thematic track — labs are all technical primitives, no threat-model-driven end-to-end design flaws.
OWASP A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures — no coverage (log injection, log evasion, audit bypass, silent-fail attacks).
OWASP API3:2023 BOPLA (Broken Object Property Level Authorization) is only partly covered by mass-assignment labs — property-level read leakage (e.g., writable fields exposed via PATCH) is missing.

OWASP API6:2023 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows has only 1-2 labs — needs signup-abuse, checkout-flood, coupon-farming-as-a-service, referral-abuse tracks with rate-limit and anti-automation gates.
OWASP API9:2023 Improper Inventory Management is only touched via one 'v1 downgrade' lab; missing forgotten sandbox subdomains, staging environments, retired public endpoints, orphaned SDK versions.
Passkey / WebAuthn coverage is a single rpId-downgrade lab; missing credential-registration CSRF, cross-device sign-in phishing, WebAuthn extension abuse, resident-key exfil.
Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner injection is missing (referenced by user prompt as a gap) — only pull_request_target and workflow_run are covered.
No gRPC / gRPC-web or Protobuf-shape confusion labs.
No WebTransport / QUIC extension attacks (only one HTTP/3 CL smuggling lab).
No Server-Sent Events (SSE) attack track beyond one auth-bypass lab (missing SSE injection, unbounded stream DoS, cross-tenant subscription leaks).
No ChatGPT plugin / OpenAPI schema-abuse or MCP-tool-poisoning labs.
No essential-skills / recon on-ramp lab (Burp intro, HTTP methods, response headers) — new users have no landing pad below apprentice.
No dedicated Cache Poisoning DoS (CPDoS) track — cache-key normalization + status-code poisoning is only partly covered.
No Trusted Types / SRI / CSP-Level-3 nonce-strict-dynamic bypass coverage as a progression.
No modern browser-side isolation attack track (COOP/COEP/CORP bypass, Spectre-in-browser via SharedArrayBuffer, cross-origin timing via performance.now).
security_risks: MOVEit Homage (sqli elite) reproduces a still-actively-exploited 2023 CVE — shipping a working exploit chain as a Docker image likely triggers vendor legal complaints and can be repurposed against real customers who haven't patched.
FortiClient EMS Homage (sqli elite) reproduces recent Fortinet header-SQLi-to-RCE — same distribution-of-exploit risk; may violate Fortinet EULA if any decompiled code is included.

LayerSlider Homage (sqli elite) reproduces an unauthenticated blind SQLi in a live commercial WordPress plugin still sold today — high risk of being used as a mass-scan template against real installs.

cve-web-2024-2026 as an entire category directly homages named vendor CVEs (Confluence CVE-2022-26134, Log4Shell, Telerik, SAML XSW, F5 hop-by-hop, VPN cookie CI, Progress-flavor bugs). Even labeled 'homage', many are 1:1 exploit primitives — this is close to distributing weaponized PoCs.

HTTP/2 Rapid Reset (CVE-2023-44487) as a lab is essentially a DoS PoC that can be pointed at any HTTP/2 endpoint; the lab even asks the solver to compute the stream-open/RST_STREAM ratio needed. Ship only in a firewalled, offline-only mode.

'ELITE CHAIN: pull_request_target + workflow_run to steal CI runner secrets' teaches a working GHA supply-chain attack — the technique is reusable verbatim against real public repos; needs strong ethical-use framing and offline sandboxing.

'ELITE CHAIN: DNS rebind to docker:2375 for full host RCE' exposes a live dockerd on TCP by design and demonstrates host escape — if the lab image is ever run outside its VM isolation the primitive escapes the lab.

Dependency Confusion labs (multiple categories) require a mock registry — if the lab's postinstall/exfil target is misconfigured or the operator forgets to bind-mount /shared, a solver's malicious package can hit the operator's real npmjs.org or PyPI.

GDPR-flavored labs seed PII into containers (SSNs, addresses, emails, chart data). Verify only synthetic data is used, seeded deterministically, and check that lab exports don't accidentally include real training-data fixtures.

Prompt-injection labs that hit 'assistant posts responses to http://oob-listener:9000/answer' — if the LLM is a real hosted model (OpenAI/Anthropic API) rather than a local mock, exfil targets and prompts leak into third-party logs.

Elite: BYO Gadget in deserialization asks the solver to author novel gadget chains against shipped source code — the resulting chains are reusable against other production Java apps; also complicates grading (need a safe verification oracle).
OAuth/OIDC labs that seed real Google/Microsoft/Okta client IDs would violate provider ToS — verify all IdPs are self-hosted mocks (Keycloak, mock-oauth2-server).
SAML labs that ship real signed responses from any commercial IdP would violate vendor terms — must use lab-generated keypairs only.
The Elite Chain SAML XSW + XSLT c14n divergence lab is directly weaponizable against real SSO deployments; document offline-only operation.
IMDSv1/IMDSv2 labs must not point at real 169.254.169.254 accidentally — a solver's misconfigured curl can reach the host EC2 if the lab image is ever run on AWS metal without host-network isolation.

The 'Isolated-vm, Not Really' lab claims a host escape from isolated-vm sandbox chained with prototype pollution — if that path really works, this is a live n-day for isolated-vm users; coordinate disclosure before publishing.

The vm2 escape (CVE-2023-30547) — vm2 is deprecated with public advisory, ok to ship, but pin the exact vulnerable version and refuse to accept the WAF-bypass variant as a template for attacking other sandboxes.
'Full E2E chat clone: unauthenticated pubkey directory' — the technique is reusable against Signal-like reference designs; annotate that this is a design flaw, not a real Signal bug.
educational_flaws: hackerone-2024-2026 has only 3 apprentice labs (postMessage XSS, NoSQL Type Juggling, Negative-Quantity Refund) — below the 5-lab on-ramp threshold; new learners drop straight into practitioner-level HTTP/2 smuggling.
ctftime-web-2024-2026 has only 4 apprentice labs — below on-ramp threshold; the track jumps to practitioner-heavy CTF-style puzzles.

cve-web-2024-2026 has only 4 apprentice labs (Nested Archive, phpinfo, Log Viewer Traversal, Migration Tool Admin Reset) — below on-ramp threshold; also the category itself is inherently expert-flavored, so an on-ramp is important.
hackerone-2024-2026 has only 2 elite labs (HTTP/2 CL.0 Smuggling + H2 CRLF Cache Poison) — below the 3-lab red-flag threshold; needs 1-2 more full-kill chains.
yeswehack-intigriti-2024-2026 has ZERO explicit elite labels — its top-tier is 'expert'. Track has no capstone chain lab; below the 3-elite red-flag threshold.
ctftime-web-2024-2026 has only 1 elite lab (WebAssembly Bounds-Check) — below 3-lab red-flag threshold.
cve-web-2024-2026 has ZERO explicit elite labels — every top-tier is 'expert'. Below the 3-elite red-flag threshold.
No orientation / recon / Burp-fundamentals lab exists at any level — the whole platform assumes users can proxy, replay, and read a Docker log.

Bug-bounty-flavored tracks (hackerone / yeswehack / ctftime / cve) heavily duplicate techniques from the earlier topical tracks; without cross-linking, learners repeat the same JWT/NoSQL/proto-pollution playbook 3-4 times.

Several apprentice labs conflate 'apprentice difficulty' with 'complex enterprise-grade scoring' (e.g., apprentice sqli 'Column Discovery via ORDER BY' requires SQLSTATE-error extraction of current_user — this is practitioner-level in PortSwigger terminology).

The label 'Blind XXE via OOB DNS Callback' is filed as practitioner in ctftime-web but as apprentice-adjacent (Silent Fetcher) in ssrf — the exact same primitive is graded inconsistently across tracks.
Business-logic (race-and-logic) apprentice labs assume familiarity with Turbo Intruder / single-packet, which are practitioner tools — the on-ramp gap is unmentioned.
The GraphQL-API track lacks a beginner Introspection-Only lab that doesn't also require BOLA/CSRF chaining.
feasibility_flags: Multiple .NET/Windows labs (BinaryFormatter Rides Again, ViewState Without a MAC, .NET XmlDocument XXE, .NET MSXML XSLT Embedded Script, Predictable Machine Key, Upload Handler .NET Deserialization, MSSQL Header SQLi to RCE) require Windows Server containers — each 2-4 GB image, cannot run on Linux Docker hosts natively, requires Windows build/runner infrastructure. Not viable for a lightweight single-image lab platform.

Elite Chain: DNS Rebinding to Unauth Kubernetes API + Pod Creation and Kubelet-on-10250 SSRF both require a functioning k8s control plane + kubelet in-container; kind/minikube in Docker is 1 GB+ each and slow to boot. Impractical for per-lab isolation.

ELITE CHAIN: DNS rebind to docker:2375 for host RCE requires exposing a docker daemon inside the lab, which is itself a sandbox-escape primitive. Requires DIND with careful cgroup/network isolation — not a small-image build.

Elite Chain: gopher to Redis Master-Replica RCE via Module Load requires a cross-arch .so shipped inside the fake-master container matching the victim Redis's arch/glibc; feasibility is deployment-fragile.
HTTP/2 Rapid Reset (CVE-2023-44487) needs both patched AND unpatched HTTP/2 server versions co-hosted; ratio measurement is timing-flaky in CI/graded environments and false-positives easily.
Spring Boot Actuator + SpEL heapdump-to-secret lab requires a live heap dump (typically 100-500 MB) plus Eclipse MAT or similar tooling in-image; heap dump generation is nondeterministic.
ffmpeg HLS Concat + Video Transcoder ffmpeg HLS SSRF require ffmpeg-full (400+ MB with all codecs); transcode jobs are slow and CPU-heavy.
WeasyPrint + Cairo + Pango + mock IMDS + mock STS + mock S3 chain in one image is a multi-service stack; WeasyPrint's font/rendering deps alone push image size past 500 MB.
SAML XSW / XSLT canonicalization labs need a real signing IdP; SimpleSAMLphp is ~200 MB PHP+Apache, Shibboleth is heavier.
Log4Shell Reproduced needs a bundled marshalsec LDAP referral server + a hosted class + Java runtime with vulnerable Log4j — 3-container orchestration for one lab.
Fastjson AutoType Ladder same: needs marshalsec LDAP + JVM + specific fastjson version — 3-container orchestration.
vm2 sandbox escape and isolated-vm escape both require version-locked Node runtimes; users may hit npm supply-chain drift if not fully vendored.
'Model Registry Munch' + Elite BYO Gadget both require ML/gadget-inspector tooling inside the image — heavy Python dependencies and unclear grading oracle for BYO chains.

Multiple 'admin bot' Puppeteer/headless-Chromium containers across dozens of labs — each Chromium container is 250-350 MB. Running 20+ solver sessions concurrently is memory-prohibitive without shared bot infrastructure.

HTTP/2 CL.0, TE.0, H2.CL, H2.TE, and single-packet-race labs require paired frontend/backend containers with specific reverse-proxy versions (HAProxy, nginx, Envoy, ATS) — each pairing needs custom Dockerfiles and is fragile against version drift.
QUIC/HTTP/3 downgrade smuggling lab: turnkey HTTP/3 stacks in Docker don't exist; requires custom quiche or nghttp3 build.
The 'Elite Chain: Currency + Race + Marketplace Takeover' implies at least 3 services + a lock coordinator (Redis/etcd) — heavy for a single lab image.
Sqli 'Out-of-Band Exfiltration on Oracle via UTL_HTTP' requires a real Oracle DB container — Oracle Database images are 2 GB+ and have restrictive licensing.

MSSQL xp_cmdshell reenablement is stated as 'Windows container' but SQL Server on Linux does support xp_cmdshell as of 2019+ — if you swap to Linux MSSQL you can drop Windows containers here; description should be corrected either way.
WordPress-based labs (WP Legacy Plugin phar://, WP-Like Plugin eval REST, Weak Nonce Role Uplift) each need WordPress + MySQL + PHP — ~800 MB per image; consider a shared WP base.
'E2E chat clone' requires two synthesized user clients + partner user + directory service simultaneously — complex orchestration for a single lab session.
IMDSv2 header-dance labs require both a mock EC2 IMDS (with TTL enforcement) and paired mock S3/STS credentials-serving service — complex.
'Seeded admin bot' cadence is inconsistent across labs (3s, 20s, 60s, 1min, per-page-load) — with 500+ labs, a shared bot-cadence spec should be mandated.

Pin exact upstream versions in each lab: Log4j (2.14.x?), fastjson (which pre-1.2.83?), vm2 (3.9.16 for CVE-2023-30547), Nginx/HAProxy/Envoy/ATS for each smuggling pairing, Node llhttp for chunked-encoding lab, php-cgi for best-fit glyph lab.
Specify which SAML IdP (SimpleSAMLphp vs mock-saml vs shibboleth) and which OIDC provider (Keycloak vs mock-oauth2-server vs custom) for every SSO lab so image size and grading are consistent.

Specify the shared OOB collector contract (URL scheme, retention window, whether flag validation is by exact path match or by extracted param) — currently oob.lab:9000, http://collector:9000, http://oob-listener:9000, http://oob:9000, http://attacker:9000, and http://collab:9000 are all used interchangeably.
Specify admin-bot cadence, browser, and cookie policy uniformly (Chromium version, headless vs headful, cookie SameSite defaults, HSTS state).
Windows-container labs must call out the Windows base image (mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore) explicitly, plus estimated image size and the fact that these cannot run on Linux daemons.
For all IMDS-flavored labs, specify the exact mock IMDS server (moto, localstack, or custom) and the credential rotation cadence.
For all K8s-flavored labs, specify whether the environment is kind/k3d/k3s/microk8s and expected image size.

Rescope real-CVE-homage labs to explicitly parody the vuln without shipping working payloads against currently-supported vendor products (MOVEit, FortiClient EMS, LayerSlider, Progress WhatsUp).
